topic: Pilates for men: more than stretching

slides.headline: Think Pilates is just stretching?
slides.sub: Clinical Pilates is strength training on springs. Plenty of blokes find it humbling.

slides.title: It's resistance training, just quieter
slides.body: Reformer springs add load in both directions, so muscles work while lengthening and shortening. You can train legs, trunk and shoulders with real resistance, minus the clanging plates.

slides.title: Control is the hard part
slides.body: Moving slowly through full range is often harder than it looks. Plenty of strong gym-goers are surprised how much a controlled single-leg press or side plank variation asks of them.

slides.title: It fills gaps the gym misses
slides.body: Heavy lifting often skips rotation, single-leg control and strength at end range. Pilates can build those qualities, which carry over to running, golf, footy and lifting itself.

slides.title: A good fit around niggles
slides.body: If your back, hip or shoulder is grumbling, springs let you keep training while the load is adjusted. Clinical Pilates is guided by an assessment, so the program suits your body.

slides.title: You don't need to be flexible
slides.body: Tight hamstrings and a stiff back are reasons to start, not reasons to stay away. Flexibility usually improves as a side effect of moving through more range with control.

slides.headline: Ready to try the springs?
slides.body: Our Pilates team starts with an assessment, then builds a program around your training and goals. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Think Pilates is just stretching? Plenty of blokes change their mind after one session.

Clinical Pilates is resistance training on springs. The reformer loads muscles as they lengthen and shorten, and the slow, controlled pace is often tougher than it looks. It also covers things heavy lifting can skip: rotation, single-leg control and strength at the end of your range.

It's a practical option when a back, hip or shoulder niggle is making the gym awkward, because load can be adjusted spring by spring. And no, you don't need to touch your toes to start.
